intro: Hinduism does not have one single holy book. It has a whole library. Some texts are hymns. Some are long stories. Some are talks between a teacher and a student.

In this unit you will learn how Hindus sort these texts. You will learn about shruti, "what is heard," and smriti, "what is remembered." You will also learn how the texts traveled for thousands of years, first by memory and later on palm leaves, in comics and on screens.
By the end, you will be able to name the main Hindu texts. You will be able to say which group each belongs to. You will be able to explain how people kept them alive.
bigQuestion: How have Hindus kept a great library of sacred texts alive for thousands of years?

timeline.t: Scholars date the oldest Rig Veda hymns to about now (c. 1500–1200 BCE)
The oldest Upanishads begin to take shape (c. 800–500 BCE)
The two great epics grow over many centuries (c. 400 BCE–400 CE)
Many Puranas take shape over the following centuries
Kamban retells the Ramayana in Tamil (date debated)
Swami Vivekananda speaks about Hindu texts in Chicago
Amar Chitra Katha comics begin retelling the stories
The Ramayana TV series airs in India
UNESCO honors the tradition of Vedic chanting

words.d: "what is heard"; the Vedas and Upanishads
"what is remembered"; the epics, Puranas and other texts
a seer; one of the ancient sages who, Hindus hold, heard the Vedas
"knowledge"; one of the four oldest Hindu sacred texts
a shruti text of teachings, often a talk between teacher and student
a very long poem about heroes and great deeds
a book of old stories about gods, goddesses, kings and the world
"the eternal way"; a name many Hindus use for their tradition
the ancient language of most early Hindu texts
spoken or passed on by mouth, not written

test.why: The Vedas and Upanishads are shruti.
The epics and Puranas are smriti.

test.q: Who do Hindus hold heard the Vedas?
test.why: Hindus hold that ancient seers, the rishis, heard the Vedas.
The Rig Veda is the oldest.

test.q: What do the Upanishads call the one reality behind everything?
Who does tradition credit with the Mahabharata?
test.why: Tradition credits Vyasa with the Mahabharata.

test.q: Where is the Bhagavad Gita found?
test.why: The Gita is part of the Mahabharata.

test.q: Which Purana tells of Krishna and Govardhan Hill?
test.why: The Bhagavata Purana tells that story.

test.q: What language are most early Hindu texts in?
test.why: Most early texts are in Sanskrit.

test.q: How were the Vedas passed down for centuries?
test.why: The Vedas were passed down orally.

test.q: What did the chanting patterns do?
test.why: Patterns like krama and ghana worked like a checking system.
Tulsidas wrote this Hindi Ramayana in the 1500s.
Many Hindus call their tradition Sanatana Dharma, "the eternal way."

test.q: Which is true of Hindus and their texts?
choices: All Hindus read only one book
test.why: Hinduism's library is large, and families and groups have different favorites.

write.prompt: Is it better to think of Hindu scripture as one book or as a library? Use two texts from this unit, such as the Rig Veda, Chandogya Upanishad 6.13 or Bhagavad Gita 2.47. Say which group each belongs to and how Hindus have used it.
tips: Name each text you use, with its chapter if you know it.
Say whether it is shruti or smriti.
Write "Hindus believe" or "many Hindus" when you tell a belief.
Use at least three words from this unit.
